key_insight: PathMem adds a cognition-aligned memory transformation to pathology MLLMs so they can explicitly encode and retrieve structured domain knowledge (taxonomy, grading, clinical evidence) and link it to visual findings, producing more interpretable diagnostic reasoning.
problem_solved: MLLMs for computational pathology lack mechanisms to integrate formal, structured medical knowledge and to produce traceable, interpretable memory traces that link morphological evidence to diagnostic and grading criteria.
method: Introduce a cognition-aligned memory transformation module that encodes taxonomy, grading rules, and clinical evidence as structured, queryable memory representations.
Link visual features extracted from pathology images to memory nodes for dynamic retrieval and alignment with diagnostic criteria during reasoning.
Provide interpretable read/write traces so the MLLM’s diagnostic steps can be inspected and mapped back to formal criteria and evidence.
impact: Enables pathology MLLMs to produce diagnoses that are better aligned with clinical protocols and easier to audit, improving trust, reproducibility, and practical deployment in clinical workflows.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: slide image → visual encoder → cognition-aligned memory transformation → MLLM reasoning → explainable diagnosis
Memory graph schematic: nodes for taxonomy, grading criteria, and clinical evidence with links to image features
Case example panel: annotated pathology image with highlighted morphological evidence and the model’s stepwise, criteria-linked reasoning
Trace/attention heatmap: visualization mapping retrieved memory nodes to the parts of the image and final diagnostic labels
paper_title: PathMem: Toward Cognition-Aligned Memory Transformation for Pathology MLLMs
paper_authors: Jinyue Li, Yuci Liang, Qiankun Li, Xinheng Lyu, Jiayu Qian
